html:
Roman general and builder, the closest friend and right-hand man of Augustus. He won Augustus's wars while Augustus did the politics.

He came from an ordinary family and grew up with Octavian. He built the fleet that beat Sextus Pompey in 36 BCE, and he commanded at Actium in 31 BCE, the battle that made Octavian master of Rome.

He also rebuilt the city's water supply. He repaired old aqueducts such as the Aqua Marcia, built new ones including the Aqua Virgo, which still feeds the Trevi Fountain, and put up the first public baths. He built the first Pantheon; when Hadrian rebuilt it, he kept Agrippa's name on the front, where it still stands (see Pantheon rebuilt).

Augustus married him to his daughter Julia, and their sons were adopted as Augustus's heirs, though both died young. Agrippa died in 12 BCE. Through his daughter Agrippina the Elder he was grandfather of Caligula and of Agrippina the Younger, and great-grandfather of Nero.
sum: Roman general and builder, the closest friend and right-hand man of Augustus. He won Augustus's wars while Augustus did the politics.
